scope: Proposition 4.4 (Entry timing, escape, and flow estimates) of the manuscript “Generic C1 Future Inextendibility Near Rotating Subextremal Kerr Spacetimes” (preprints/Generic-C1-Future-Inextendibility-Near-Rotating-Subextremal-Kerr-Spacetimes-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 702eacef09cb6165), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On either prepared end use regular exterior time te, co-moving coordinates y, and lab coordinates z = y + Ce(te), with fixed sup |C′ e| ≤ s∗ < 1/10, after decreasing ϵ if needed. The relevant slice te = 0 agrees with the original bridge sufficiently far out. There is a preparation parameter I with 0 < cI ≤ I′ ≤ CI and I(tT ) = T. The launch patch near v = x = T on S occurs at te = tT + O(1), and tT ≍ T. A fixed enlargement is contained in te ≤ tT + C2. Its selected-end portion v < (1 − ν0)T is earlier by at least cν0T − O(1) for each fixed ν0 > 0. The exterior metric has uniformly regular spacelike temporal levels. Its first and second ordinary lab derivatives are bounded on the computing region and become arbitrarily small at sufficiently large co-radius, uniformly in time. Every fixed mixed jet on the used time and radius ranges O(1 + T) is eo(T). Entry charts have a noncharacteristic collar with controlled low jets and subexponential fixed higher jets; the inner exit has a strict margin deeper than the entry cylinder. The null covectors dv launched on a sufficiently small fixed patch at this entry escape towards the past to the same original end. For each fixed β > 0, after fixing a sufficiently large radius and taking T large, their bridge arrival points satisfy (1 − β)tT < |z − z∗| < (1 + β)tT , z∗ = Ce(tT ). (4.11) The entry crossing is unique and transverse, and separated from other used ray portions outside a uniform collar. Every fixed Hamiltonian flow jet, including launch-center derivatives and the propagators on all subsegments, is eo(T). Tensor parallel transport and its inverse are bounded. These assertions hold on short past and future launch enlargements through the deeper exit.
